The authors consider pressure-driven microflow of a power-law fluid with constant but unequal heat fluxes imposed at the upper and lower walls.
The dimensionless slip coefficients at the lower and upper walls are denoted as K1 and K2, respectively.
The power-law index n is taken to be either 0.5 (shear-thinning) or 1.5 (shear-thickening).
The modified Brinkman number Br' is kept constant at 0.2 in the analysis.
Asymmetric slip shifts the location of the velocity maximum closer to the wall with larger slip coefficient.
Asymmetric slip redistributes the peaks and plateaus of the Bejan number profile across the microchannel.
For the same slip coefficient, the Hatzikiriakos slip law predicts a higher Nusselt number and less entropy generation compared to the asymptotic slip law.
Entropy generation is primarily due to fluid friction in shear-thinning fluids, while it is primarily due to heat transfer in shear-thickening fluids.
Higher Br' leads to increased entropy generation, and can cause the Nusselt number to become negative for shear-thickening fluids.
The difference in the imposed heat fluxes leads to starkly different Bejan number profiles depending on which wall is hotter.
Asymmetric slip is shown to promote uniformity in both the velocity field and the temperature field, thereby reducing irreversibility in the flow.
The results are relevant to microfluidic devices, unconventional energy applications like hydraulic fracturing, and other industrial processes involving non-Newtonian fluids and slip flow.
The authors derive exact analytical expressions for the velocity profile, temperature distribution, Nusselt number, and entropy generation rate.
The study considers the effect of asymmetric slip on heat transfer enhancement and reduction of entropy generation in pressure-driven non-Newtonian microflows.
The authors use Navier's nonlinear slip law to model the asymmetric slip boundary conditions at the channel walls.
